05e25292b259.text: Two independent routes to the same answer, for two counters that are busy half the time. The left route counts the states: three equal bars, each marked one third, for both counters free, one counter free, and both counters busy. The first two carry a tick and the third a cross, and a line beneath reads tick served at once, cross waits. The right route runs the Erlang B recursion instead: B of one equals one half, B of two equals one fifth, one minus rho times one minus B equals three fifths, and C equals one fifth divided by three fifths. An arrow from each route meets in a single box at the bottom reading C of two and one equals one third, one arrival in three waits.
05e25292b259.evidence: VIS: one-line-or-many-figure2.png - the drawing has exactly three equal bars each labelled 1/3 (both free, one free, both busy), ticks on the first two and a cross on the third, the key line tick served at once cross waits, the recursion column B(1) = 1/2, B(2) = 1/5, 1 - rho(1 - B) = 3/5, C = (1/5) / (3/5), and one box at the bottom reading C(2, 1) = 1/3, one arrival in three waits. CALC: M/M/2 at a = 1 gives pi0 = 1/(1 + 1 + 1) = 1/3, pi1 = 1/3, P(n >= 2) = 1/3 - three equal thirds, as drawn. 2feba65ffd1f.text: Two weighted averages drawn on one left-to-right scale of success rate, with no numbers. The upper line belongs to the option that leads in both groups: its two group rates are marked as open circles, and both of them sit further right, that is higher, than the matching circles on the lower line. Its pooled figure is drawn as a square and sits close to its left-hand circle, because most of its trials ran in the harder group. The lower line belongs to the option that trails in both groups: its pooled figure is drawn as a diamond and sits close to its right-hand circle, because most of its trials ran in the easier group. Dashed lines drop from both pooled marks to the scale, and the diamond lands further right than the square. So the option that trails on both lines wins the pooled total, and the mark sits wherever the trials sat.

f8d607b598a5.text: Two time charts of the same four customers at the same two counters, drawn one above the other against a shared minute scale from zero to eight. Customer A takes six minutes; B, C and D take two minutes each. In the upper chart, labelled one line, counter 1 runs A from minute 0 to 6 while counter 2 runs B, then C, then D, back to back, finishing at minute 6. Nothing is left waiting while a counter stands empty, and the longest anyone waits is four minutes. In the lower chart, labelled a line per counter, A and C joined counter 1 and B and D joined counter 2. Counter 1 runs A from 0 to 6 and then C from 6 to 8, while counter 2 finishes D at minute 4 and then sits empty, marked idle, from minute 4 to minute 8. C is still waiting when that empty stretch begins, and the longest wait is six minutes instead of four.

DEF: "Only CV 1.00 leaves both exact."는 참이다 — CV≠1이면 95퍼센타일이 언제나 맞춘 지수 꼬리라 정확하지 않고, CV=1이면 M/M/c의 평균도 대기시간 분포도 정확하다. 창구가 하나면 CV≠1에서도 **평균만** Pollaczek–Khinchine으로 정확한데, 문장이 is exact가 아니라 leaves both exact라 그 경우를 잘못 말하지 않는다. CALC: 그 두 값(평균·95퍼센타일)을 946상태 전부에서 Fraction + Erlang C 닫힌 형태로 다시 계산해 카드·표의 12,298개 숫자와 모두 같았다.
